modes.name: write_without_confirmation
modes.definition: issue_refund or cancel_order is called without a prior turn in which the agent showed the matched order (product title, store, price, status) and the user confirmed it by selecting the order widget or stating that order's number. Applies to every role, whether or not the user supplied an order identifier in the request. A bare yes, a product name, or a description does not count as confirmation.
modes.boundary: Nearest: assumes_instead_of_asking. That mode is about ambiguity of the request; this one fires on any write that lacks the confirmation turn, even when the request was unambiguous and the order id was given. Absent: agent shows the order, user replies with that order number (or selects the widget), agent writes. Also absent: agent shows the order and asks, and no write follows (0124, 0020, 0082, 0011 t0). Asking for a product name instead of the order number is a weaker ask (0191, 0029) but still not this mode while no write happens. Tightened 2026-09-21 from 'explicit yes' to 'order number or widget'.
modes.spec_source: RESP-6 (new 2026-09-19, widened 2026-09-20, confirmation form tightened 2026-09-21): show the order, confirm by widget or order number, then write

modes.name: assumes_instead_of_asking
modes.definition: The request or the lookup result is ambiguous (several plausible orders, unclear complaint) and the reply proceeds on one interpretation instead of asking the user which one.
modes.boundary: Nearest: write_without_confirmation and unwarranted_escalation. 'Proceeds' means any action on one interpretation: a reply, a lookup fan-out, a ticket, or a write. A write on a single unambiguous match is write_without_confirmation only; when the action is a ticket, label both. Asking the user which one (0011, 0120) is absent.

modes.name: unwarranted_escalation
modes.definition: escalate_to_human is called (a) before the target order or the complaint details have been confirmed with the user, (b) when the request was already resolved by a successful tool result, (c) when the refund is already queued_for_approval, which is itself the human review, or (d) for a required escalation, without first gathering the details the ticket needs to be resolved.
modes.boundary: Nearest: unsolicited_next_steps (an offer in text vs. a ticket actually created) and assumes_instead_of_asking (the ticket is the action taken on an unconfirmed interpretation; label both when both apply). Escalations the situation requires are absent: inconsistent record (0017, ESC-3), past-window exception a merchant asks for (0042, 0015, ESC-4). Records that are internally inconsistent (reversed dates 0152, 0230; store mismatch 0017, 0169) require escalation under ESC-3; for those, only clause (d) can apply.
modes.spec_source: ESC-3, ESC-4 (escalation is for what the agent cannot resolve)

modes.boundary: Nearest: none in the reply layer; this is a tool-use mode. modes.name: unsolicited_next_steps

modes.name: verbose_reply
modes.definition: The reply either (1) states the same fact or instruction more than once in one turn, or (2) includes policy mechanics, caveats, or background the user did not ask about and that are not needed to answer the question (beyond the answer, one citation, and one sentence of context).
modes.boundary: Nearest: unsolicited_next_steps (offers of further action) and irrelevant_policy_nuance (the specific override mention). verbose_reply covers repetition and unrequested explanation, not offers of action and not the override sentence alone.

modes.name: first_person_framing
modes.definition: The reply frames a system rule or outcome as the agent's personal decision or ability in the first person ('I can't cancel it', 'I found', 'I'm not authorized') where the rule, the record, or the policy is the actual reason.
modes.boundary: Nearest: verbose_reply. This mode is about the framing of one sentence, not its length. 'I opened a ticket' for an action the agent actually took is absent; 'I can't refund this' for a policy outcome is present. Empathy or casual-judgement notes (0001, 0104) are not this mode and stay parked.
modes.spec_source: RESP-5; candidate SPEC guidance: state rules and outcomes impersonally

modes.name: no_reference_date
modes.definition: The reply asserts a date-based conclusion (a return or refund deadline has passed or not passed, or a time span the user described does or does not match an order) that contradicts or explains away a tool result or the order record, such as refund_eligible or ordered_at. Root cause found in HW4: the prompt gives the agent no current date, so it guesses today.
modes.boundary: Nearest: assumes_instead_of_asking (the agent resolves an ambiguity by guessing; here the guessed value is today's date, and the guess overrides a tool field rather than the user's intent). Absent: a deadline computed and stated as a date with no claim about whether it has passed; a past/future claim that agrees with the tool's eligibility flag; a mismatch claim the user later confirms.
modes.spec_source: RESP-7 (new, 2026-09-21): the agent receives the current date and makes every date claim relative to it; RESP-3 covered the invented value meanwhile
modes.notes: Promoted to final on 2026-09-21 (ninth mode, above the handout's 5 to 8 range by reviewer decision). From Workshop Part C, W1.

modes.name: incomplete_outcome_report
modes.definition: A reply that reports the result of issue_refund or cancel_order, or answers an order status question, omits one or more of the required fields: the order (number, product, store), the amount or status, what happens next (auto-approved, queued for human review, cancelled), and the expected timing. Applies whether or not the user asked for a short answer.
modes.boundary: Nearest: verbose_reply (too much) and first_person_framing (how the outcome is phrased). This mode is about too little: the required facts are missing, however short or long the reply. A short reply that contains all required fields is absent (0021). All four positives so far follow a 'short plain answer' request, so the boundary with 'the user asked for brevity' matters: brevity removes filler, not the required fields.
modes.spec_source: RESP-8 (new, 2026-09-21): required fields in outcome and status replies; ESC-1 (the agent explains the result)
modes.notes: Promoted from backup mode incomplete_write_outcome on 2026-09-21 (tenth mode, above the handout's 5 to 8 range by reviewer decision). Widened from write confirmations to status replies after 0056.
